title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Educational Planning and Management (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Educational Planning and Management (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: If a high school student drops out of school before completing secondary schools, what is the financial implication of this incident?
options: This will save the budget since those school dropouts are using the school resources any longer
This will have no impact on the cost of education
The unit cost of the remaining students will be higher
He/she can use the knowledge and skills gained for further study and better employment, hence, no wastage at all
questions.explanation: The unit cost of the remaining students will be higher due to a smaller number of students sharing the fixed costs. When a student drops out, the fixed costs of running the school (facilities, teacher salaries, etc.) remain the same, but are now distributed among fewer students.

questions.questionText: A Public school budget includes the following except:
questions.explanation: An educational plan is not typically included in a public school budget. Public school budgets generally include revenue plans (funding sources), capital outlays (infrastructure and equipment), and expenditure plans (operational costs), but the educational plan is a separate document that guides curriculum and instruction.

questions.questionText: School management is different from hospital management in that it requires different set of:
questions.explanation: School management requires a different set of technical skills compared to hospital management. While both require leadership and management capabilities, the technical skills in education (curriculum, pedagogy, student assessment) differ significantly from those needed in healthcare (medical procedures, patient care, health regulations).

questions.questionText: Prioritizations of projects involve the ranking and selection of projects. This idea excludes:
options: The 'best' projects are moved actively into the design
Number of people affected by the project be high
Geographic area affected by the project
No need to compete for support and resources
questions.explanation: There is always a need to compete for support and resources in project prioritization.

questions.questionText: Which one of the questions is irrelevant when planners sit for preparing the plan document?
options: How are we going to get there?
Why do we waste time by doing so?
Where do we want to go?
questions.explanation: The question 'Why do we waste time by doing so?' is irrelevant to the planning process.

questions.questionText: Assessing the benefits of education involves an inquiry into the following questions except:
options: What knowledge, skills, and attitudes are gained by the learners?
Are the graduates the type of people that can create new things?
Is the community getting any service from graduates?
How do graduates help in solving community problems?
questions.explanation: The question 'Is the community getting any service from graduates?' is not typically part of assessing educational benefits in the traditional sense. This is actually more related to community impact assessment rather than direct educational benefit assessment, which focuses on knowledge, skills, attitudes, innovation capacity, and problem-solving abilities of graduates.

questions.questionText: Which one the following is not the potential benefits of participative leadership?
questions.explanation: Participative leadership does not lessen accountability for leaders.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements conveys an incorrect idea about change management?
options: It is an approach of transition individuals, teams, and organizations to the desired state
It may involve strategic, transformational, & top-down approaches
It is the art to design and manage the transition as painless as possible
It may be initiated by lower level managers
questions.explanation: The statement 'It may be initiated by lower level managers' conveys an incorrect idea about change management. Significant organizational change is typically initiated by top management or middle management with proper authority, rather than lower-level managers who generally lack the necessary resources and organizational power to implement widespread change.

questions.questionText: As an instrument of planned change at schools, strategic planning serves the following purposes except that it helps schools:
options: To cope with the rapidly changing environment
To be proactive; perceiving problems beforehand
To achieve the best fit between the school and its environment
To be reactive, taking actions on problems at hand
questions.explanation: Strategic planning is meant to be proactive, not reactive.

questions.questionText: For a normal distribution of (Z) test for independent the basic assumption not used is:
options: Measurements are on an interval scale.
Over thirty subjects in each group
Statistical mean be the same in values
questions.explanation: The assumption that 'statistical means be the same in values' is not a basic assumption for Z tests. In fact, Z tests are often used to determine if means are different. Basic assumptions for Z tests include: measurements on an interval scale, normally distributed populations, and sufficient sample size (typically n>30).

questions.questionText: Given the goal of survey research is to provide a numerical description of phenomena, which one is not correct?
options: Involves the gathering of limited data
Particular cases are tested under laboratories
It shows prevailing conditions of particular trends
questions.explanation: Survey research does not typically involve testing particular cases under laboratory conditions.

questions.questionText: Suppose you are given with a raw score of 40 students in a class for math test out of 100. What is the range of scores you obtain?
questions.explanation: The range is calculated as the difference between the highest and lowest scores. Without actual data for the 40 students' scores, this question cannot be answered accurately. The correct answer (60) must assume specific highest and lowest scores in the dataset.

questions.questionText: Job descriptions, as a function of human resource management,
options: Contains information on the organizational historical setup
Contains detailed information about the job
Contains information on the past achievement of the organization
questions.explanation: Job descriptions provide detailed information about the job.

questions.questionText: The 1994 Ethiopian Education and Training Policy states that:
options: Mother tongue is used for instruction in primary and secondary schools
School leaders will be selected from the teachers
Parents are expected to cover tuition fees for their children
questions.explanation: The 1994 Ethiopian Education and Training Policy emphasizes the use of mother tongue for instruction, particularly in primary education. This was a significant shift to promote learning in students' native languages and preserve linguistic diversity, though in practice it was primarily implemented in primary schools rather than secondary schools.

questions.questionText: The type of statistics used to say something about a set of information that has been collected only is termed as:
questions.explanation: Descriptive statistics summarize and describe the characteristics of a data set.

questions.questionText: Employee work performance does not depend on:
questions.explanation: Race should not influence employee work performance.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct match.
options: Human skill - the ability to use social media
Human skill - ability to use laboratory facilities
Conceptual skill - Ability to see organization as system
questions.explanation: Conceptual skills involve understanding the organization as a system.

questions.questionText: Who among the list can be considered a person of serious researcher?
options: Data collection for money as in private consultancy
The urge to solve immediate social problem through investigative report
Making some writing to get known in the neighborhood
To answer for official request from government
questions.explanation: A serious researcher is characterized by the urge to solve immediate social problems through investigative reports. This motivation focuses on knowledge creation and problem-solving rather than financial gain (option A), personal fame (option C), or merely fulfilling official requests (option D). True research is driven by the desire to address significant questions and contribute meaningful solutions.

questions.questionText: Specifically, micro planning has to do with fulfilling of the choices given below except:
options: To meet to work for dropout decrease
To actualize the needs and aspirations of students
To take share of the demand to access to education
To meet efforts of government for school expansion
questions.explanation: Micro planning is not specifically focused on dropout decrease. While decreasing dropout rates may be a beneficial outcome of good micro planning, the primary focus of micro planning is on fulfilling local educational needs, student aspirations, increasing access to education, and implementing government expansion initiatives at the local level.

questions.questionText: Supply management, at school level, refers to those activities involving:
questions.explanation: Supply management includes warehousing activities.

questions.questionText: Often for all, there should be a research method used. What is not the right naming?
questions.explanation: Tools piloting is not a recognized research method. It is a procedure or technique within research methodology used to test and refine research instruments, but it is not classified as a distinct research method like descriptive, experimental, or historical methods.

questions.questionText: Given the subject matter of economics of education as very dynamic, the practice cannot be for:
options: The 20 century human capital formation economic theories
Public & private rate of return of education
questions.explanation: The practice of economics of education cannot be solely based on 20th century human capital formation theories because the field is dynamic and continually evolving. Relying exclusively on older theories without incorporating newer developments would be inadequate. The other options (rates of return, income distribution, and public investment) remain relevant areas of study in contemporary economics of education.

questions.questionText: Organizations are different from other human collections in that:
options: They survive irrespective of the service they offer
They cease to exist when their managers are changing.
They require both qualified and unqualified personnel to achieve their goals.
Their existence is justified by their goals.
questions.explanation: Organizations exist to achieve specific goals.

questions.questionText: Education policy statement needs to provide for the following except:
questions.explanation: The history of educational leaders is not a necessary component of an education policy statement.

questions.questionText: Policy impact assessment in public institutions exclude:
options: Listing of changes that still need to be accomplished
Listing of positive and negative changes
Cost - Benefit Analysis: How much a financial gain has a change made?
questions.explanation: Cost-benefit analysis is not typically excluded from policy impact assessment. In fact, it is often an integral part of evaluating policy effectiveness. The answer appears to be incorrect, as all four options are commonly included in comprehensive policy impact assessments.

questions.questionText: A good example of a project physical investment generally includes:
questions.explanation: Purchasing equipment and supplies is a direct physical investment.

questions.questionText: Efficiency in education can be stated as:
options: Achieve the desired output with a minimum inputs or resources
School graduates with many dropouts due to resource abuse
Higher enrolments during the year due to proper financing
Education output of students at any cost of funding
questions.explanation: Efficiency is about achieving outputs with minimal resources.

questions.questionText: A school principal wants to predict using English test scores provided to students in grade nine and ten for the same batches. The coefficient of correlation calculated for the students was found to be (r = 0.8) this is indicative as:
questions.explanation: A correlation coefficient of r = 0.8 indicates a strong positive correlation between the English test scores in grades nine and ten. This high correlation suggests consistency in performance and reliable prediction, which would typically be associated with good achievers who maintain their performance levels across different grades.

questions.questionText: School mapping and micro planning ensure all but one.
options: It is a formative stage in planning
It represents the highest planning level
questions.explanation: School mapping and micro planning do not represent the highest planning level.

questions.questionText: Effective educational planning can be ensured in the absence of all except.
questions.explanation: Qualified personnel are essential for effective educational planning.

questions.questionText: What a supervisor does principally is to do with utmost care one of the following.
questions.explanation: The principal role of a supervisor in an educational context is to facilitate student learning. This is accomplished through supporting teachers, improving instructional practices, monitoring curriculum implementation, and ensuring effective teaching and learning processes. The other options (office work, replacing the deputy principal, and payroll preparation) are administrative tasks rather than the core supervisory function.

questions.questionText: For a primary school program improvement, the frequent push to project idea can be:
options: Damages caused from droughts or floods
High demand for child entry to schools
questions.explanation: High demand for child entry to schools can drive program improvement.

questions.questionText: Unlike the following position holders, the school instructional leader is rather similar to.
questions.explanation: The school instructional leader is most similar to a cluster schools team leader, as both roles focus on educational leadership, instructional improvement, and supporting teaching and learning within educational institutions. The other options (zonal inspection team, health center head, and kebele desk team supervisor) represent different sectors or functions that are less aligned with instructional leadership in schools.

questions.questionText: For planning to start needs analysis has to be made first. Which one idea is not the basis for the study?
options: Being mandatory while it is being performed
most senior planner does not need it
The status, competencies, and interests of those persons in the study
Organizational units performing the needs analysis
questions.explanation: A senior planner should still consider needs analysis.

questions.questionText: In project creating, which one is not a common analysis technique used in educational planning.
options: Analysis of school drop-out and output
questions.explanation: Fundraising from the public is not a common analysis technique used in educational planning. It is an implementation activity for securing resources, not an analytical method. In contrast, calculating enrollment rates, analyzing dropout patterns, and comparing curriculum development techniques are all legitimate analytical approaches used in educational planning to assess needs and design appropriate interventions.

questions.questionText: A public school organization, as a social entity, contains:
questions.explanation: Public school organizations are purpose-driven entities.

questions.questionText: If a principal says 'I have the right qualities to be a leader' he assumes to fall under that of:
questions.explanation: Trait theory focuses on the qualities of the leader.

questions.questionText: For instructional leaders to be effective, the possession of desired quality is achieved through the following except:
options: Courage of furnishing his office beyond the plan
questions.explanation: Courage to exceed the plan is not a necessary quality for instructional leaders.

questions.questionText: Effective micro planning and school mapping work deals mainly with assessment of the essential resources should be within reach. If so, which one is incorrect?
options: Inventory of resources in the library
Inventory of active teachers in the year
questions.explanation: An inventory of malfunctioning lab equipment is not useful for effective micro planning and school mapping. While it might be part of maintenance planning, effective resource assessment for micro planning typically focuses on functional resources that can be utilized (library resources, active teachers, and usable teaching materials) rather than items that are broken or non-functional.

questions.questionText: The elements of organizational culture exclude:
questions.explanation: Profit margins are not an element of organizational culture.

questions.questionText: Many planners think micro planning cannot waste time on one of the following:
questions.explanation: Creating a national vision is not a primary focus of micro planning and would be considered a waste of time at this level. Micro planning focuses on local implementation rather than national strategy development. National vision setting is typically a macro planning function, while micro planning is participatory, action-oriented, and bottom-up in nature.

questions.questionText: In a primary school where 2000 students are enrolled, the total annual fixed cost amounts Birr 95000, and the variable cost amounts Birr 30000. What is the unit cost?
questions.explanation: Unit cost is calculated as total costs divided by the number of students. Total costs = Fixed costs + Variable costs = 95,000 + 30,000 = 125,000 Birr. Unit cost = 125,000 ÷ 2,000 = 62.5 Birr per student.

questions.questionText: Which one the following represents group behavior?
questions.explanation: Group dynamics refers to the behavior of groups.

questions.questionText: Making jobs more rewarding by adding more meaningful tasks is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: Job enrichment involves adding meaningful tasks to a job.

questions.questionText: An effective education policy making process is:
options: Bureaucratic and technocratic in its approach
questions.explanation: An effective education policy making process should be participatory.

questions.questionText: During planning you consider the effect of globalization to some degree? What cannot be an issue?
options: Psychological nature of being black or white
questions.explanation: The psychological nature of race is not a direct issue in educational planning.

questions.questionText: Abraham Maslow (1954) identified five basic groups of human needs that emerge in a specific sequence or pattern - that is in a hierarchy of importance. Identify the correct hierarchy of needs.
options: Physiological Needs, Safety needs, esteem needs, social needs, self-actualization needs
Physiological Needs, Safety Needs, Social needs, esteem needs, self-actualization needs
Physiological Needs, esteem needs, social needs, safety needs, self-actualization needs
Physiological Needs, Social needs, safety needs, esteem needs, self-actualization needs
questions.explanation: The correct hierarchy according to Maslow is: 1) Physiological Needs (basic survival needs like food, water, shelter), 2) Safety Needs (security, stability), 3) Social needs (love, belonging, relationships), 4) Esteem needs (respect, recognition), and 5) Self-actualization needs (personal growth, fulfilling one's potential).

questions.questionText: Inspection is rather an exercising of authority and control. This specific role is classified as:
questions.explanation: Inspection is a line function as it involves direct authority.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following occurs before the others in the managerial communication process?
questions.explanation: Encoding occurs first in the communication process.

questions.questionText: Educational supervisors help in the training of staff empowerment. Isolate the one not applicable.
options: Use violence approach when in difficulty
Persuaders by argument to do the right thing
Be able to influence the affairs of the community
Give the moral bases for teacher autonomy
questions.explanation: Using violence is not an acceptable approach in staff empowerment.

questions.questionText: The process of reviewing human resources requirements to ensure that the organization has the required number of employees, with the necessary skills to meet its goals, is known as:
questions.explanation: This process is referred to as human resources planning.

questions.questionText: It is sometimes delicate to strike the optimum balance between simplicity and effectiveness of a project means:
options: To use local low cost or imported techniques and materials
Component being elaborated is not too complex.
Choice to replace broken-down classrooms or to repair them
Construct buildings on forced account or to bring in contractors
questions.explanation: Striking the optimum balance between simplicity and effectiveness means ensuring that project components are not too complex while still being effective. This involves finding the right level of sophistication that achieves project goals without unnecessary complications that can impede implementation or sustainability. The other options describe specific decisions rather than the core principle of balancing simplicity with effectiveness.

questions.questionText: The essentials of good leadership exclude:
questions.explanation: Political party membership is not essential for good leadership.

questions.questionText: A planned change excludes:
questions.explanation: The computer system itself is not a planned change.

questions.questionText: If you want to work on the training needs of individual staff, you may ask the following questions except:
options: What past achievement she/he has scored for the organization?
What does the employee have to do?
What particular knowledge, skills, and level of training does he/she needs?
questions.explanation: Past achievements are not directly relevant to current training needs.

questions.questionText: Which one the following is not the advantage of group decision making?
options: It serves as a forum for representing group interests
It gives a room for autocracy of the majority
It increases the acceptance of the decision made
It enhances democratic rights of employees in an organization
questions.explanation: Group decision making should not lead to autocracy of the majority.

questions.questionText: An individual behaves at work is influenced by the following except:
questions.explanation: Gender should not influence behavior at work.

questions.questionText: The usual purpose of educational research is all but one:
options: Description to identify the state and nature of the problem
Providing common information heard from close friends
questions.explanation: Providing common information from friends is not a purpose of educational research.

questions.questionText: There is a clear similarity between projects and programs except in one:
questions.explanation: The key difference between projects and programs is that projects typically have a limited time span with clear start and end dates, while programs tend to be ongoing or have a much longer duration. Both projects and programs use geographic space, serve target groups, and require allocated funds, but their temporal nature differs significantly.

questions.questionText: Of the following, planning cannot ignore equity issues in the country.
options: The distribution of the benefits to all
Stated distribution is 'just' for the population
Fair share of costs across all regions
School construction biased to central regions
questions.explanation: The statement 'School construction biased to central regions' represents an inequitable approach that should not be part of educational planning. While the other options reflect proper equity considerations in planning (fair distribution of benefits, just distribution, and fair cost sharing), biasing resources toward central regions creates inequity and should be avoided.

questions.questionText: Kurt Lewin's three-stage force field analyses excludes:
questions.explanation: Disequilibrium is not one of the stages in Lewin's model.

questions.questionText: Designing expenditure plan requires collection of current information as following except:
questions.explanation: When designing an expenditure plan, consulting all those concerned is not strictly required, unlike the other options which involve direct financial records. While stakeholder consultation may be beneficial for transparency and buy-in, the technical process of expenditure planning primarily relies on objective financial data such as budget records, cost accounting data, and inventory/store records.

questions.questionText: One of the following cannot be the characteristics of educational research?
options: Directed towards the solution of educational problems
Attempts to find an objective, unbiased solution
Is a deliberate and unhurried activity
questions.explanation: Educational research requires relevant expertise.

questions.questionText: The instructional leader acts as supervisor of teachers who should give immediate performance feedback. What is not expected of him in the process?
options: Visit by surprise in his/her class to supervise
Create a positive environment before engagement
Make an agreed plan of supervision well ahead of time
Disclose strengths first and then changes/corrections to make
questions.explanation: Surprise visits are not an expected practice for effective instructional leadership. Unannounced visits can create anxiety, undermine trust, and appear confrontational rather than supportive. Effective supervision typically involves scheduled observations with prior notice, creating a positive environment, having an agreed plan, and providing balanced feedback that acknowledges strengths before addressing areas for improvement.

questions.questionText: Among the following which defines research best?
options: scientific approach to study a problem
An enquiry to get trivial news
questions.explanation: Research is best defined as a scientific approach to studying problems.

questions.questionText: Some essential working competencies of a leader exclude:
questions.explanation: Acting bossy is not a competency of effective leadership.

questions.questionText: Individual sources of resistance to change include:
questions.explanation: Security concerns are an individual source of resistance to change. People often resist change because they fear it will threaten their job security or established routines. Structural inertia and limited focus are organizational sources of resistance, not individual. Threat to expertise is also an individual source of resistance, but not the answer marked as correct.

questions.questionText: Which one is unhelpful for quality assurance procedures?
options: Pupil Teacher Ratios (PTR) at school and grade level
Enrolment of Children with Special needs
Principal office facilities you can afford to have
Drop-out Rate of school and at each grade level
questions.explanation: Principal office facilities are unhelpful for quality assurance procedures as they focus on administrative comfort rather than educational quality. The other options (pupil-teacher ratios, enrollment of children with special needs, and dropout rates) are all important indicators that directly impact or reflect educational quality and student outcomes.

questions.questionText: Among the list found under this question, which can be the goal of research?
options: Develop a systematic knowledge in education
Predict and control events in educational solutions
Interpret scientifically the behavior of the different components
Use the general principles to explain to students in class
questions.explanation: Developing systematic knowledge is a primary goal of research.

questions.questionText: We make distinctions between data types. Which one can be in the category of continuous values of measurement?
questions.explanation: Numerical data can be continuous, meaning it can take any value within a range (such as temperature, height, or time). Discrete data represents counts that can only take specific values (like number of students), categorical data represents groups or categories, and 'measured data' is not a standard statistical classification but would typically fall under either continuous or discrete numerical data.

questions.questionText: Employee motivation as a managerial function is contribution of:
options: The human relations school of thought
The scientific management school of thought
questions.explanation: The human relations school emphasizes employee motivation.

questions.questionText: Whatever shape they follow, organization charts show the following except:
options: The various functional units of the organization
The official lines of chain of command
The title and salary of each manager's position
questions.explanation: Organization charts typically do not show the salary of each manager's position.

questions.questionText: According to McGregor's Theory X, the average employee:
options: Will respond as positively to work as they do to play or rest.
Shows commitment to organizational objectives is a function of rewards associated with the attainment of objectives.
Dislikes work and will do whatever is necessary to avoid it.
questions.explanation: Theory X posits that the average employee dislikes work.

questions.questionText: Which one the following is not the result of job analysis?
questions.explanation: Job rotation is not a direct result of job analysis.

questions.questionText: For macro planning purpose a thorough study is made on situations of needs and resources to achieve objectives. Which study approach is not needed in data processing?
questions.explanation: Data storing in archives is not a necessary step in the data processing phase of macro planning. While data cleaning, entry, and compilation are active processing steps that transform raw data into useful information for planning, archiving data is a post-processing activity that deals with long-term preservation rather than immediate analysis needed for planning decisions.

questions.questionText: If he thinks 'I can empower my followers to live the vision' then it is most likely to fit to:
questions.explanation: This statement aligns with transformational leadership theory.

questions.questionText: The informal organization differs from the formal organization one in that the former:
options: Fosters on the part of the members a feeling of personal integrity and of self-respect
Consciously provides for regular channels of communication
Is a system of structured interpersonal relations
questions.explanation: The informal organization fosters personal integrity and self-respect.

questions.questionText: A person in charge with the oldest controlling mechanism in the history of enterprises was named:
questions.explanation: The foreman is often considered the oldest controlling mechanism in enterprises.

questions.questionText: The incremental approach to policy making approach assumes that:
options: Only incremental and limited policy adjustments can be made
There exist agreed criteria by which solutions can be judged
The problem at hand does not go beyond man's cognitive capacities
That the problem-solvers have adequate incentives to stay with the analysis until it is completed
questions.explanation: The incremental approach focuses on small, manageable changes.

questions.questionText: School mapping and micro planning is a good example of:
questions.explanation: School mapping and micro planning are better examples of operational planning rather than strategic planning. They involve the detailed implementation of broader strategies at the local level, focusing on specific resource allocation, facility placement, and addressing immediate local educational needs.

questions.questionText: For parametric two-sample tests, the t-test is specially adapted for small samples, means:
options: One or both samples are smaller than thirty
Both samples be less than 50 subjects
questions.explanation: The t-test is used when one or both samples are smaller than thirty.

questions.questionText: Coercion as a means overcoming resistance to change excludes:
options: Facilitating the resisters request for transfer
Blocking the promotion requests of resisters
Giving poor letters of recommendation for resisters
Giving negative performance evaluations to resisters
questions.explanation: Facilitating requests for transfer is not a coercive measure.

questions.questionText: In staff performance appraisal process the problem with appraiser excludes:
questions.explanation: Constant error is not typically recognized as a standard problem with appraisers in performance evaluation, unlike the other three options which are well-documented biases. Central tendency error (tendency to rate everyone as average), halo effect (letting one trait influence overall rating), and 'different from me' error (penalizing approaches different from the appraiser's) are common appraisal biases.

questions.questionText: The minimum requirement of the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to perform a particular job is known as:
questions.explanation: A job specification outlines the minimum requirements of knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to perform a particular job. This differs from a job description, which details the tasks, responsibilities, and duties of the position rather than the qualifications needed to perform it. 'Human requirements' and 'job standard' are not standard HR terminology for this concept.

questions.questionText: As a principal if he says 'I know how my subordinates respond to my particular style of leadership in different learning environment' then it can fall under:
questions.explanation: This statement reflects situational leadership theory.

questions.questionText: Ethiopian Education and Training policy of the 1994 argues that former system was entangled with the following problems with the exception of:
questions.explanation: Public demand for education was not a problem identified in the former system.

questions.questionText: All are major parameters usually appear in the preparation of long-range planning document except:
options: Provision of sufficient to qualified manpower
Costing of the main event jobs
The right of authorities to reject main planning components
questions.explanation: The right of authorities to reject components is not a planning parameter.

questions.questionText: Principals as instructional leaders cannot be bureaucratic is to say that:
options: They lack the expertise to give proper support
They have orders to be fulfilled without question from office
They remove the barriers to leadership
questions.explanation: Instructional leaders should provide a meaningful learning environment.

questions.questionText: Which is one the following is incorrect about capital expenditure in the education sector?
options: Affects the intake capacity of schools
Too difficult for the community to cover for schools
Matches the supply and demand for education
questions.explanation: It is incorrect to state that capital expenditure is 'too difficult for the community to cover for schools.' While capital expenditures can be substantial, they are often funded through various mechanisms including government budgets, international aid, loans, and community contributions. With proper planning and resource allocation, capital expenditures are manageable.

questions.questionText: Educational planning refers simply to all expect.
options: With aim of making educational development
Maintain education as more effective and efficient
Working for past time frame in education sector
questions.explanation: Educational planning should not focus on past time frames.

questions.questionText: Education overall creates efficient and skillful human resources to increase the productivity of labor force. This idea most highly relates to:
questions.explanation: This statement most highly relates to 'Education responding to labor market' rather than 'Efficiencies in education.' It describes how education creates skilled workers to meet labor market needs and increase productivity, which is fundamentally about education's response to and interaction with the labor market.

questions.questionText: Of the following one is not inform about the concepts of economics of education as its relatively a new field of study:
options: Applies the principles, theories of economics on education
Concepts of economics used to explain only the issues of education
Concepts of economics used to explain the issues of education
Establishes cause and effect relationship among the two
questions.explanation: The concepts of economics are not limited to only education issues.

questions.questionText: In the concept of educational planning, which idea does not describe it?
options: The aim of making education more effective and efficient
Clearly responds to the needs and goals of its students and society
The application of rational analysis to the process of educational development
Marks the sense of modernizing a country in every sector
questions.explanation: Educational planning does not necessarily mark the modernization of every sector.

questions.questionText: The benefits of human resource development and training exclude:
questions.explanation: Absence of supervision is not a benefit of human resource development.

questions.questionText: Job analysis can be computed through the following activities except:
questions.explanation: Registrar archival data is not a method of job analysis.

questions.questionText: When doing the analysis of qualitative data, which one cannot be relevant?
options: Tables used to enter scaled quantities
questions.explanation: Tables for scaled quantities are not relevant in qualitative data analysis.

questions.questionText: Of the following statement, education has been concerned with 'theories of economic growth' except:
questions.explanation: Political diplomacy theory is not a theory of economic growth.

questions.questionText: For data types that are in the category of whole numbers of measurement is termed as:
questions.explanation: Discrete data refers to whole numbers of measurement. Discrete data can only take specific, countable values (like the number of students in a class) and cannot be divided into smaller increments. Categorical data represents groups or qualities, while numerical data includes both discrete and continuous values. 'Measured data' is not a standard classification in statistics.

questions.questionText: Different levels of workers require different extent of education. Which of the following is logically unacceptable?
options: One-year specialized training after school certificate for supervisors
Trained skill competence varies among same level male and females
Low profile of work comes from illiterate persons
The highest level of power of work requires university education
questions.explanation: Trained skill competence should not vary based on gender.

questions.questionText: The presence of rules and regulations, in schools, makes possible:
options: The specification of the rights and duties at each position.
Uniformity and instability in employee action
The use of more power by the school leader
Coordination of different activities outside the organization
questions.explanation: The presence of rules and regulations in schools makes possible the specification of rights and duties at each position. This provides clarity on roles and responsibilities, establishes boundaries, and creates a framework for accountability. Option B contains a contradiction ('uniformity and instability'), while options C and D misrepresent the primary purpose of organizational rules.
